cohort: The study included 100 very preterm infants (gestational age <32 weeks), where 50 infants received extra-uterine placental transfusion (EPT) and 50 received delayed cord clamping (DCC), matched by gestational age and delivery mode for singletons, and within twin pairs.
finding: In twin subgroups, extra-uterine placental transfusion (EPT) was associated with a significantly higher rate of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) compared to delayed cord clamping (DCC), while no differences were observed in overall deaths or major morbidities between the two groups.
gest_age: Very preterm infants with gestational age <32 weeks; mean gestational age for DCC was 29.16 ± 1.76 weeks and for EPT was 29.12 ± 1.84 weeks.
